title: Applying Related-Key Techniques to the GOST Hash Function
summary: Related-key techniques apply to GOST2 and a GOST-based Davies–Meyer hash, but whether they can attack the actual GOST hash function remains open.

formal_statement.body: A related-key differential for GOST based on 3-round local collisions has been developed, and the same techniques have been applied to GOST2 and to a Davies--Meyer hash function based on GOST; the unresolved task is to determine whether these techniques can be used to attack the actual GOST hash function.

scope.domain: Related-key differential cryptanalysis of GOST-family block ciphers and hash functions.
parameters: 3 rounds: length of the local collisions underlying the related-key differential
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the techniques can be used to attack the actual GOST hash function.

citations.label: Practical-Time Related-Key Attack on GOST with Secret S-boxes

progress.summary: The source reports a related-key differential for GOST based on 3-round local collisions and applications to GOST2 and a GOST-based Davies–Meyer hash. It identifies applying these techniques to the actual GOST hash function as the main open question.
citation_labels: Ariel Weizman et al., Practical-Time Related-Key Attack on GOST with Secret S-boxes
